blocking.section: Decision outcome > Consequences (line 92) and More information > Proposed owning-document amendments (line 136)
blocking.issue: This is still open from the previous re-review, and the revision did not change it. The QUIC-loss bullet says in-flight QUIC connections are also lost when a Hot Reload replaces the UDP socket, and it cites OQ-system-overview-18 for that case. That question and ADR-0015 cover only binary upgrades. The owning document promises that Hot Reload drops no in-flight request, and that a changed listener gets a new socket while old connections finish. The ADR therefore states an exception to the owning document's Hot Reload guarantee, attributes it to an Open question about a different event, and does not route it anywhere. The Data plane amendment bullet (line 136) lists HTTP/3 Bounded resources rows, the quic-go limits, StrictMaxConcurrentRequests and Alt-Svc, but not this loss. The technical claim is plausible: a new UDP socket in the SO_REUSEPORT group re-hashes existing QUIC flows. It needs to be recorded as a Data plane exception, not attached to the upgrade question.
blocking.evidence: Line 92: "- Bad, because in-flight QUIC connections on UDP 8443 are lost at a Zero-Downtime Upgrade, or when a Hot Reload replaces the UDP socket, while TCP connections Drain ([ADR-0015](0015-zero-downtime-upgrades-so-reuseport.md), OQ-system-overview-18)." Line 136: "Data plane SHOULD add HTTP/3 Bounded resources rows, an Open question on the quic-go limits and `http.ResponseController` deadline support, `StrictMaxConcurrentRequests` false in Upstream layer, and an Open question on HTTP/3 discovery (`Alt-Svc`), which the M3 HTTP/3 row depends on." System overview, Open questions: "| OQ-system-overview-18 | Can upgrades keep in-flight QUIC connections? | Accept loss (current); connection-ID steering | data-plane | No |". Foundation pack 8.4: "loses in-flight QUIC connections on a binary upgrade (OQ-system-overview-18)". ADR-0015 line 51: "| QUIC | In-flight QUIC connections on UDP 8443 are lost and reconnect (OQ-system-overview-18) | Planned (M3) |". Data plane, Summary: "configuration snapshot swaps during Hot Reload that drop no in-flight request". Data plane, Listeners and protocols: "A Hot Reload never mutates a running server: a changed listener gets a new socket and server before the swap." Data plane, Why no in-flight request is dropped, item 3: "An added listener opens before the swap; a removed one stops accepting after it while its connections finish." System overview, Request lifecycle: "**Pinned snapshot.** Each request stays on its starting snapshot through any Hot Reload."
blocking.fix: Replace line 92 with: "- Bad, because in-flight QUIC connections on UDP 8443 are lost, while TCP connections Drain, at a Zero-Downtime Upgrade ([ADR-0015](0015-zero-downtime-upgrades-so-reuseport.md), OQ-system-overview-18) and when a Hot Reload replaces an `http3` socket (amendment below)." That adds 2 words. On line 136, after "`StrictMaxConcurrentRequests` false in Upstream layer,", insert: "the Hot Reload QUIC loss with an Open question,", which adds 9 words. The body is at 1,494 of 1,500 words (verifier count), so offset the 11 words without touching text that closed earlier findings. First, remove ", so no extra module serves 8080" from line 107, saving 6 words. Second, remove the duplicate ", which KrakenD lacks ([source](https://www.krakend.io/features/))" from the Context question on line 21, saving 4 words; line 37 and line 128 still cite it. The result is 1,495 words. If more room is needed, remove " and SSE relies on `http.ResponseController` ([source](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#ResponseController))" from line 118, saving 6 words. The Chosen option sentence and the Deadlines row already source that dependency.

non_blocking.suggestion: "within the 592 KiB per-connection budget (hypothesis)" cites a Data plane figure made up entirely of HTTP/2 and TLS terms. L1-5 covers feasibility. From the consistency side, present the figure as a target that the proposed HTTP/3 Bounded resources rows must meet, not as an existing budget that QUIC already fits.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome, FIPS builds row (line 49) and Confirmation, FIPS job (line 100)
non_blocking.suggestion: "never binds UDP 8443" names only the default port. The Configuration model makes `port` required on each listener, and HTTP/3 uses UDP on the `https` port. Write "never binds UDP for an `https` listener" so that a FIPS Node with `port: 443` is covered too.

`ruralz_fips` is a feature build tag. The rule it changes is the Repository layout Build constraints rule "No feature tags (P1)". Quote that rule in the amendment bullet so the owner of that document sees the conflict.

Configuration model, Gateway: "`http3: true` is `Planned (M3)` and off in FIPS builds." That sentence can be read as the field being silently ignored, which the FIPS row rules out under pack section 8.1. Extend the amendment so it also rewords that sentence to "refused on FIPS Nodes (RZ-CFG code under OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9)".

Data plane, Upstream layer says "HTTP/2 Upstreams honor server limits through `HTTP2Config.StrictMaxConcurrentRequests`". The ADR pins the field false. The amendment on line 136 should name the sentence it replaces, so the Data plane owner treats it as a correction and not an addition.

"has no catalog row, so [Admission] rejects it" overstates the Tech stack Admission flow. That flow rejects only on G1, G2, G3 or govulncheck, and fasthttp would pass all four. What actually blocks fasthttp is the depguard deny rule proposed on line 138. Cite that rule as the mechanical check, or write "reviewers refuse a catalog row for it under Admission".

PB-8 is tagged "(target)", which matches Performance budgets, but System overview lists the same seed item as "30 or fewer (hypothesis)". The ADR follows the value owner. Route the tag mismatch to System overview conformance so the two foundation-level sources agree.

The verifier reports only WARN lines, no FAIL lines: the roadmap has no matching M5, M1 or M3 items. For line 123, removing the Planned tag from the rejected option's Bad bullet ("leaving the HTTP/3 work without a library") clears the warning. The other two warnings need roadmap entries, which are outside this document.

Every external URL in the ADR is in a research file, but most HTTP/2, quic-go and Go release URLs are only in `docs/_meta/research/go-libraries-runtime.md`, which the manifest entry does not list. Add go-libraries-runtime.md to research[].

foundation_amendments: Foundation pack section 8.4 and OQ-system-overview-18 record the QUIC connection loss only for a binary upgrade. A Hot Reload that replaces an `https` listener with `http3: true` also loses in-flight QUIC connections. That conflicts with System overview's 'Each request stays on its starting snapshot through any Hot Reload' and Data plane's 'drop no in-flight request'. Either widen OQ-system-overview-18 to 'Can upgrades and listener-replacing Hot Reloads keep in-flight QUIC connections?' or have Data plane add its own Open question, and change the section 8.4 sentence to match.

Carried forward: foundation pack section 1 (FIPS build: 'the same features and license as the default build') and vision P1 ('one feature set in every public build, including the FIPS build') should name the HTTP/3 exception that section 8.4 creates while OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9 is open. ADR-0001, ADR-0009 and the market landscape document already note it.
